segments.text: Hey everyone, today I'm sharing my honest results from thirty days of sixteen-eight intermittent fasting.
Sixteen-eight means I ate everything within an eight hour window, from noon to eight p.m., and fasted the other sixteen hours.
Before I started I talked to my doctor, because I take medication for blood pressure, and she was fine with it as long as I tracked how I felt.
The first week was rough. I was genuinely hungry every morning around ten, and by day three I had a headache most afternoons.
What fixed it was drinking a lot more water and adding a pinch of salt to it, and by day six the hunger basically went away.
Energy-wise, I was tired the first few days, but in week two I actually felt more focused in the mornings than before.
A lot of you asked about the eating window, so I want to talk about timing for a second.
I picked noon to eight because it fits my work schedule, and dinner with my family is at seven, so I never had to skip it.
Some people do ten to six instead, and honestly the exact window matters less than being consistent every day.
To break my fast I usually had two eggs, Greek yogurt with berries, and a big glass of water, around twelve fifteen.
I avoided breaking the fast with something sugary because the one time I had a pastry I crashed hard an hour later.
Okay, results. I started at one hundred eighty two pounds and on day thirty I weighed one hundred seventy four.
So that's eight pounds down in a month, and my waist measurement went down about an inch and a half.
I want to be transparent, though: in the month after I stopped being strict, I gained about three pounds back.
So the net is closer to five pounds, which I'm still happy with, but it's not magic.
Is it safe? For me it felt completely safe, and honestly I think pretty much anyone can do this.
That said, if you're diabetic, pregnant, or have a history of eating disorders, please do not start this without talking to a doctor first.
My friend who is type one diabetic tried it and had a scary low blood sugar episode, so this is not for everyone.
Workouts: I kept lifting three times a week, and I trained around four p.m., inside my eating window, never fasted.
Strength stayed about the same, which surprised me. I thought I'd lose a lot more.
Would I do it again? Probably, but more like five days a week, not every single day.
Thanks for watching, drop your questions below and I'll answer them in the next video.
